summary:
G3 English review of GQUR-300 Unit 2 (Numbers and Operations) against the bound course guide, content spec, coverage matrix, sources, figure manifest, concept graph, style guide and contracts. All 96 bound inputs digest-verified against the prepared manifest at commit 235af7b with zero mismatches, and the bound tree was clean at the start and end of the review. All three cited sources were retrieved and read this session: the NCC mathematics page and both PDFs it serves (the Grades 1-8 Suggested Guidelines, text-decoded from CID glyphs, opens with the Number and Operations domain; the NCP Mathematics Progression Grid 1-12, National Curriculum of Pakistan 2022-23, Domain A Numbers and Operations with integers, ratio, proportion and percentage SLOs), the OpenStax Prealgebra 2e table of contents (every cited chapter and section exists exactly as cited, authors, 2020, CC BY confirmed), and the ERIC record for Gula and Lovric (2025), whose abstract confirms every claim the verification excerpt makes.

Disposition is revise, with four blocking defects, each with a precise location and repair.

First, fig-U2-1's side note '0 counts as a whole number' is clipped about 100px past the SVG's 780px viewBox in both the light and dark variants: the text is anchored at x=696 and its glyph box runs to x=880. Three independent measurements agree (in-browser getBBox on the served SVG, scripts/measure-figure-text.mjs, and pixel analysis of the rendered element screenshot), and check:figures passes because it measures no glyph geometry. A learner cannot recover the note's content.

Second, the unit's flagship misconception, scaling by adding, is self-refuting at the numbers chosen: the recipe serves 20 people with 6 spoons of sugar, the friend adds 6 spoons for 20 more people, and 6 + 6 = 12 is exactly the correct 6 x 2 for 40 people, so the recipe is not broken and the ratio is not destroyed. The supplied model answer nonetheless asserts that adding destroys the ratio. The defect runs through the misconception paragraph, the topic check-your-understanding item, RRQ-06 and its model answer, and the teacher-notes sherbat demonstration, which would produce two identical-tasting batches at a doubling.

Third, gula2025 is cited only in topic-03's Further reading and appears nowhere in unit prose, contradicting sources/unit-02.md's own claim that every key is cited both in prose and in a per-topic Further reading section.

Fourth, the concept graph maps CON:GQUR-300-2-7 (proportion as equal ratios, checked by cross-products) to RRQ-05, which is the atlas percentage-discount item and assesses a different concept; the cross-product check is taught in topic-02 prose but assessed by no item in the bank.

Everything else the rubric asks for holds: all four guide leaves are taught and assessed, the MCQ key agrees with independent derivation on 10 of 10 items, all five ERQ rubrics are arithmetically sound and sum to their stated totals, the 10/10/5 blueprint and per-topic floors are met, the register is accessible to a fresh HSC graduate, activities are feasible with stated group sizes and timings, and narrow-viewport and A4 print layout are clean with figures and answers intact. Advisory findings: the teacher notes call 42/60 the raw score that 'looked biggest' when 55/75 is the largest raw score; both NCC citations read n.d. although the Progression Grid's own title page is dated 2022-23; the content-spec key terms Root and Operation are not carried as glossary entries while the other ten are; and 9 of the 10 RRQs restate topic check-your-understanding or worked-example items, so the summative bank adds little beyond the formative cycle for those items.

Recorded for the parent, outside this unit's bound inputs: the production build (npm run build) fails at this commit on GQUR-300 unit-03 MDX (bare < and <= parsed as JSX at topic-01.mdx:141, topic-02.mdx:70, unit-assessment.mdx:72). Unit-03 is not bound to this review and every unit-02 page compiles; the render inspection therefore ran against the Docusaurus dev server, which serves the same reviewed bytes for unit-02. Unit-03 needs its own repair before the site can build statically.

This report is advisory. It is unsigned, no qualification record or protected registry entry exists for this reviewer, and nothing here certifies the unit, activates a reviewer, or writes a tracker row.

FAILURE 1 - RRQ-06 is unsound as posed and its model answer states a falsehood. The recipe serves 20 people with 6 spoons of sugar (topic-02 classroom situation); the friend's '20 more people, so add 6 more spoons of sugar' gives 6 + 6 = 12 spoons for 40 people, which is exactly the correct 6 x 2 = 12, and adding 4 spoons of tea the same way preserves the ratio (12:8 = 3:2 = 6:4). The recipe is not broken, yet the item asks trainees to 'explain the error' and the model answer (unit-assessment.mdx:176-179) asserts 'adding keeps the difference constant while destroying the ratio', which is false at a doubling. The same self-refuting numbers appear at topic-02.mdx:55-58 (misconception paragraph), topic-02.mdx:98-99 (Check your understanding 5) and unit-teacher-notes.mdx:45-47 (sherbat demonstration). The additive-scaling misconception is real but only fails visibly when the multiplier is not 2.

The content-spec's other two listed misconceptions ('a percentage is a separate kind of number', 'division of fractions has no meaning') are addressed structurally - percentage taught as a ratio out of 100 and as one of three notations of one idea (fig-U2-3), fraction division given a concrete metre meaning (fig-U2-2) - though not as named callouts; recorded, not counted a defect.

PASSING - teacher notes are substantive: three-week sequencing with reasons, four misconceptions to probe with concrete classroom moves, activity-running guidance including the deliberate sign-error entry, and marking guidance that names the bank's deliberate traps.

FAILURE - the add-to-scale misconception correction is self-refuting at the numbers chosen. topic-02.mdx:55-58 presents '20 more people, so 6 more spoons of sugar' as the error to correct, but for a 20-to-40 doubling the additive answer equals the multiplicative one (12 = 6 x 2), so the worked misconception demonstrates nothing: a trainee who checks the arithmetic finds the friend is right, and the paragraph's claim that adding destroys the ratio is false at these numbers. The teacher-notes sherbat demonstration (unit-assessment.mdx RRQ-06 and unit-teacher-notes.mdx:45-47) would mix two identical-tasting batches. The repair is to move to a non-doubling case (for example 30 more people: adding gives 12 spoons where 15 are needed), which makes the error visible; the general principle (multiply, never add) needs no change.

findings.message: Clipped figure text: static/img/figures/gqur-300/unit-02/fig-U2-1.svg (and the bound dark twin fig-U2-1.dark.svg) anchor the side note '0 counts as a whole number' at x=696 in a 780-wide viewBox; the glyph box runs to x=880, so roughly the last 100px of the note is cut at the figure boundary in both light and dark themes. Verified three ways: in-browser getBBox on the served SVG (logs-agent-g3-gqur300-u2-run001/fig-U2-1-browser-geometry.txt), scripts/measure-figure-text.mjs ('overflows right edge by 100.3px', exit 1, logs-agent-g3-gqur300-u2-run001/measure-figure-text.txt), and pixel analysis of the rendered element screenshot (glyphs present in the final 8 columns at the note's rows). A learner cannot recover the note. npm run check:figures exits 0 because it measures no glyph geometry. REPAIR: re-anchor or shorten the note in both SVGs - the Urdu variant fig-U2-1.ur.svg already uses a safe placement (x=84, text-anchor end) that the English repair can mirror - then re-run node scripts/measure-figure-text.mjs on both files until clean.

Self-refuting misconception example and unsound model answer: the add-to-scale misconception is presented with the one multiplier (2) at which adding the original amount is correct. The recipe serves 20 people with 6 spoons of sugar; the friend's '20 more people, so add 6 more spoons of sugar' yields 12 spoons for 40 people, which equals the correct 6 x 2, and adding 4 spoons of tea the same way preserves the ratio 12:8 = 3:2, so the recipe is not broken. Locations: docs/semester-1/gqur-300/unit-02/topic-02.mdx:55-58 (misconception paragraph, 'Adding the same amount keeps the difference constant, but recipes need the ratio constant'), topic-02.mdx:98-99 (Check your understanding 5, 'Explain in two sentences why this breaks the recipe'), unit-assessment.mdx:110-111 (RRQ-06 stem) and 176-179 (model answer asserting the ratio is destroyed), unit-teacher-notes.mdx:45-47 (sherbat demonstration, which would produce two identical-tasting batches at a doubling). REPAIR: change the crowd increase to a non-doubling (for example 30 more people: add gives 12 where 15 are needed) consistently across all five locations, keeping the multiply-never-add principle; the model answer's ratio-vs-difference explanation then becomes true as stated.

Citation traceability broken for gula2025: specs/content/gqur-300/sources/unit-02.md:3-5 asserts 'every key here is cited both in prose and in a per-topic ## Further reading section', but Gula and Lovric (2025) appears only in the Further-reading block at docs/semester-1/gqur-300/unit-02/topic-03.mdx:149-151 and nowhere in unit prose; the claim it is recorded as supporting (U2-06, numeracy tasks as their own category, distinct from word problems and modelling) is not made in the prose either, while coverage/unit-02.md grounds U2-06 in this key. The source itself was retrieved (ERIC EJ1489427) and its abstract supports the substance. REPAIR: cite Gula and Lovric in topic-03's prose where the daily-life applications framing rests on it (for example at the '### Applications of numbers and operations in daily life' opening, attributing the numeracy-task framing), or correct the sources-file claim and re-ground U2-06 on openstax-prealgebra alone.

False assessment linkage in the concept graph: specs/content/gqur-300/concepts/unit-02.md:24 maps CON:GQUR-300-2-7 'Proportion as equal ratios, checked by cross-products' to RRQ-05, but RRQ-05 is the atlas percentage-discount item (25 percent off a 640-rupee atlas in two ways) and assesses CON:GQUR-300-2-9 (percentage as a ratio per hundred), which also lists it. The cross-product check is taught at topic-02.mdx:42-44 but assessed by no item anywhere in the bank, so the row overstates assessment coverage. npm run check:concept-graph exits 0 because it checks ID resolution, acyclicity and orphan-freedom, not semantic linkage. REPAIR: either add an RRQ that actually checks a proportion by cross-products and point the row at it, or set the row's Assessment item IDs to '-' ; do not leave RRQ-05 on this row.

Inaccurate superlative in the teacher notes: docs/semester-1/gqur-300/unit-02/unit-teacher-notes.mdx:60-61 says 'the raw score that looked biggest (42/60) performs worst', but 55/75 is the largest raw score (55 > 42) and performs mid-table (73.3 percent); 42/60 is the second-largest raw score and the weakest performer. The ERQ-04 stem's 'which raw score looked most impressive but performed worst' (unit-assessment.mdx:137-139) has the same looseness. REPAIR: reword to 'second-largest raw score' or 'large-looking but weakest'.

Citation date: both unit citations read '(NCC, n.d.)' on the owner-approved reasoning that the NCC landing page asserts no publication year, but the retrieved Progression Grid's own title page is dated 'National Curriculum of Pakistan 2022-23' (sources-agent-g3-gqur300-u2-run001/ncp-mathematics-pg-1-12-extracted.txt). The citation could carry the document's own date. Owner call; not blocking.

Unglossed declared key terms: specs/content/gqur-300/content-spec.md '## Unit 2' declares ten key terms; eight plus Exponent and Square root are carried as bilingual glossary entries, but 'Root' and 'Operation' are not (verified against glossary.json). 'Root' is effectively covered by the Square root entry; 'Operation' is used throughout topic-03 without a glossary wrapper. REPAIR: add glossary entries or note the substitution in the spec.

Summative bank reuses formative material: 9 of the 10 RRQs restate topic check-your-understanding or worked-example items (RRQ-01/02/03/06/08/10 verbatim; RRQ-04/05/07/09 same structure and numbers as the topic's examples), and ERQ-01/02/03 restate the three topic Summative tasks verbatim. No contract requires novelty and the bank does sample the whole unit, but a trainee who worked the formative cycle has already met most of the summative band. REPAIR opportunity at the same time as the RRQ-06 fix: vary surface features (contexts or numbers) on the re-used items.

Outside this unit's bound inputs, recorded for the parent: the production build fails at this commit on GQUR-300 unit-03 MDX - bare '<' and '<=' in prose are parsed as JSX by MDX v3 (docs/semester-1/gqur-300/unit-03/topic-01.mdx:141, topic-02.mdx:70, unit-assessment.mdx:72; npm run build exit 1, logs-agent-g3-gqur300-u2-run001/build.txt). Unit-03 is excluded from this review's manifest by ADR-0027 scoping and every unit-02 page compiles and renders, so this review's render inspection ran against the dev server over the same reviewed bytes; but the site cannot build statically and CI's FULL_GATES will fail until unit-03 escapes its '<' characters. Expected non-content command failure, recorded so it is not mistaken for a unit-02 defect.
